label: Scheduled Utilisation (SU)
definition: The provider changes its import or export at times fixed when the trade is agreed. Only delivered energy is paid (GBP/MWh); there is no availability payment.

label: Peak Reduction (PR)
definition: The provider lowers its peak power over a period agreed at trade, rather than delivering continuously. Only delivered energy is paid.

label: Operational Utilisation (OU)
definition: The DNO instructs the provider in real time, usually after a network event, and pays only for energy delivered. Variants differ by maximum response time (2 or 15 minutes).

label: Scheduled Availability + Operational Utilisation (SA+OU)
definition: The DNO buys availability windows at trade, which cannot be changed afterwards, and then instructs utilisation within them. Availability is paid in GBP/MW/h and utilisation in GBP/MWh. DNOs also write SAOU or OUSA.

label: Variable Availability + Operational Utilisation (VA+OU)
definition: Like SA+OU, but the DNO can refine which availability it needs closer to the time (week ahead, or month ahead for the week-ahead variant). DNOs also write VAOU or OUVA.
